angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 506,470 km at 21.56 pc = 0.31 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 46.3763 +/- 0.0221 mas (same row, RUWE 1.02): 21.56 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.728 +/- 0.008 solar radii from Ellis et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 97658 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..118E/abstract): 506,470 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.85 +/- 0.08 solar masses from Ellis et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 97658 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..118E/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5212 +/- 43 K from Ellis et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 97658 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..118E/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Ellis et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 97658 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..118E/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-97658.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.643, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
